summary: Find the one element that appears once in a sorted array where all others appear twice, in O(log n).
mainInsight: Before the single element, pairs start at even indices (nums[2k] == nums[2k + 1]); after it, the pairing shifts to odd indices. Binary search on even indices: if nums[mid] equals its partner, the single element is to the right, otherwise it is at mid or to the left.

approaches.name: Binary search on pair parity
approaches.summary: Compare nums[mid] with the partner at mid ^ 1.

commonMistakes: Not forcing mid to be even
Using nums[mid + 1] without a bounds check

promptVariants: How does binary search locate the single element?

options: Pairs start on even indices before it and on odd ones after
The single element is always the middle element of the array
The values before it are smaller than the values after it
The sum of the left half is even before the single one
cards.answer: Pairs start on even indices before it and on odd ones after
cards.explanation: Check whether nums[mid] pairs with its even-aligned partner.

incorrectOptionExplanations.The values before it are smaller than th: Sortedness does not tell where the single lies.
incorrectOptionExplanations.The sum of the left half is even before: Sums do not locate it reliably.

promptVariants: What does a match imply about where the single element is?
cards.answer: mid ^ 1 is the partner index if pairs are aligned (even index with the next, odd index with the previous). If nums[mid] == nums[mid ^ 1], everything up to mid is correctly paired, so the single element lies to the right; otherwise it is at mid or to the left.
keyPoints: Match => single is to the right
Mismatch => single at mid or left
